title: Remote Device Repair
outcome: Diagnose configuration, storage, network, and application faults and apply bounded fixes
breakthrough: Support can repair devices without full remote control
lane: Device, mobile, enrollment, build, and edge delivery

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Remote Device Repair Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Remote Device Repair Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed entities, capabilities, jobs, events, state transitions, and outputs required to diagnose configuration, storage, network, and application faults and apply bounded fixes, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for mobile devices, sensors, secure enrollment, application delivery, remote repair, and edge execution; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Remote Device Repair Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: diagnose configuration, storage, network, and application faults and apply bounded fixes.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Remote Device Repair Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Remote Device Repair Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using device profiling, sensor fusion, predictive maintenance, workload scheduling, and network adaptation.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Remote Device Repair Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the device map, mobile console, sensor stream, build-to-device panel, and remote repair view, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Remote Device Repair into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Remote Device Repair Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Remote Device Repair Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: Support can repair devices without full remote control. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.
